question: Right to Protection of Life and Personal Liberty is given under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 21**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that **no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law**.
 
• This article is a part of the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed by the Constitution.
 
• It ensures the protection of life and personal liberty for every individual in India.
 
• The right to life under Article 21 is not merely confined to animal existence but extends to the right to live with human dignity.
 
• Article 21 has been interpreted broadly by the Supreme Court to include various derivative rights like the right to privacy, right to a clean environment, and right to health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 20**

 
 
• Article 20 deals with the protection in respect of conviction for offences.
 
• It provides safeguards against arbitrary and excessive punishment to an individual who is accused of a crime.
 
• It includes provisions related to ex-post-facto laws, double jeopardy, and protection against self-incrimination.
 
 
 
• **Article 22**
 
 
• Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
 
• It guarantees the rights of individuals who are arrested to be informed of the grounds of their arrest and to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.
 
• It also includes provisions for preventive detention laws.
 
 
 
• **Article 23**
 
 
• Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labor.
 
• This article aims to abolish practices such as human trafficking, begar (forced labor without payment), and other similar forms of forced labor.
 
 
 
• **Right to Privacy**
 
 
• The right to privacy has been recognized as a part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• In the landmark judgment of *Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd) vs Union Of India* (2017), the Supreme Court declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right.
